sentences.text: Gwalior Bench : Dated : 23.08.2022
Shri Rajmani Bansal, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri B.P.S. Chauhan, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.

Heard on I.A.No.12673/2022, first application under Section 397 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of petitioner.
This criminal revision assails the judgment dated 05.08.2022 passed by the Fourth Additional Session Judge, District Guna (M.P.) in Cr.A.No.273/2016 whereby petitioner has been convicted u/S. 2 (ix) (k), 7 (ii), 16 (1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to suffer imprisonment of 6 months with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.

entities.text: Fourth Additional Session Judge, District Guna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that trial Court as well as appellate Court erred in convicting and awarding the jail sentence of six months of simple imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1000/- with default stipulation.

In fact, petitioner is well within his HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Criminal Revision No.3021/2022 (Ritesh Jain Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh) limit when he sold tea in open manner rather than misrepresenting any brand for the same, court below erred in convicting the petitioner as per the Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,1955.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Criminal Revision No.3021/2022 (Ritesh Jain Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Petitioner already suffered 18 days' incarceration and is diabetic and heart patient.
He undertakes to cooperate.
Applicant further undertakes to perform community service to purge his misdeeds, if any, by way of plantation and to serve national/ environmental/ social cause voluntarily
Under these circumstances, he prayed for suspension of the jail sentence of petitioner and grant of bail.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the documents appended thereto.

Considering the submissions and looking to the fact that petitioner already suffered 18 days'
incarceration, this Court intends to allow this application. I.A.
